_what: How read-data/speak.mjs (tool:say-with-a-voice-model and tool:voices) speaks in a natural voice made by a speech model on the person's own computer. Nothing goes to a paid service. `programs` are the programs that run a speech model, tried in order (the one the person gave as `speech_python`, else the first whose `check` program is found on `search_path`, else on PATH); `run` starts do-work/speak-with-mlx.py once for each request, in the run's own folder. `engines` are the speech models: `takes` says what makes the voice (a person's `reference` recording and its exact words, or a model's own `speaker`). `voices` are the voices every person has without making one, each kept as a row of the person's own Voices list the first time their voices are listed. A person's own voices, which voice they chose and every speed are rows of their own lists (`lists.voices` and `lists.places`, kept through the run's records door), with each reference recording in `person.folder` of their files. A place with no voice uses the chosen voice; a place with no speed uses its voice's speed, else `speed.default`, always within `speed.min` and `speed.max`. A sound is made at its natural pace and answered with the place's speed, which the player applies with the pitch kept. A voice is said with the voice asked for, else the person's chosen one, else each of `voices` in order; when none can run, the answer is an error with every reason. `make` picks a reference from any recording of the person: the stretch, between `window.shortest_seconds` and `window.longest_seconds` long and nearest `window.best_seconds`, that starts after a pause and ends where a sentence ends with a pause after it, heard with `make.hear_model`, because a reference cut mid-sentence makes a model say its last words before the text. `loudness` brings every voice to one level. `keep` is where a said sound is kept in the person's files, so any of their devices plays it. Moved from the product repo's computer/speak.json, the speech-program and speech-engine rows of records/speech-engine-records.json, the Voices and places lists of src/voices.json and the speed scale of parts/ui/show/speed-control/speeds.json.

voices.label: Voices
voices.about: The voices Trillion can speak to you in, and how fast each one talks. The one marked Chosen speaks wherever a place names no voice.

fields.label: Speaker
fields.free_text_because: The speech engine's own speaker id the voice is made with (one of the engine's built-in speakers), written by the device that makes the voice, not a person.

places.label: Where Trillion speaks
places.about: Each place Trillion talks to you or for you, the voice it uses there and how fast. A place with no voice uses your chosen voice; one with no speed uses that voice's speed.
